title: Limit shapes for centrally excited walks
status: The Lean formalization subsection now describes the formalization of this version, and the bibliography file is renamed oct23-references.bib. Every other line, the 22 statement blocks included, is that of oct13.tex.
scope: Original Bou-Rabee–Peres theorem statements and order. No additional generalized model or additional theorem.
simplifications: Singh exit-time stopping proves coarse bounds before the deterministic-time argument.
Directional crossing proof shortened under its original deterministic hypotheses.
Dynkin formula for a squared Green function replaces convolution and resolvent estimates.
Backward radial integration bounds the curvature term directly and removes its iteration.
Shared covariance calculations and a single geometric comparison shorten the limit-law and lower-bound proofs.
Exponential-deviation proof rewritten by external Opus with the original statement retained.
The deterministic pointwise comparison and cell estimate precede probability bounds.
One all-dimensional exterior local-time estimate and one shared cap/near-far/crossing proof replace the separate outer-radius arguments.
Authorized removal of unused interval conclusions in Lemma 3.1; the former potential approximation is retained verbatim.
Convexity and one quadratic test function replace mollification and the radial comparison in the cell estimate.
The coarse lower bound integrates over an inner ball rather than deriving and integrating a uniform exit profile.
One projection estimate at integer radii replaces two separate supporting-plane crossing arguments.
The outer-radius proof bounds the Newtonian integral first, then uses one cap bound and one width estimate in all dimensions.
One maximum-principle argument gives the uniform potential bound in both the plane and higher dimensions.
Coarse occupation alone supplies the variance bounds needed for polynomial radius tails.
One spatial split replaces dimension-specific weighted-moment estimates for separated-site covariances.
One annulus supplies both logarithmic radius lower bounds.
One Taylor expansion at the fixed site replaces the origin calculation followed by translation.
One precise martingale CLT/LIL statement replaces repeated verifications in the three applications.
Replace the two author-approved auxiliary crossing lemmas by one exponential-distance expectation argument grouped by departed site.
Use the distance estimate simultaneously in time at a deterministic horizon, removing projection-direction geometry and level counting.
Compress standard kernel, cell, and dyadic-annulus calculations while keeping the potential mechanism.
Use the squared-Green Dynkin identity directly, retaining the planar shift and energy absorption.
Shorten norm-radius algebra, ray integration, cap estimates, and the Young substitutions in the Euclidean outer bound.
Compress covariance sums, martingale limit-law applications, conditional exponential moments, and fluctuation tail substitutions.
Retain the explanations, title, four authors, principal statements/order and five figures; repair references to removed intermediate labels and proof steps.

last_prose_only_revision.scope: Lean formalization subsection rewritten to state that this version is formalized; bibliography file renamed to oct23-references.bib.
last_prose_only_revision.old: The theorems, lemmas and propositions of the version of this work by \citet{BouRabeePeres2026CERW} were formalized in Lean~4, building on Mathlib. Their statements are those of this paper, except that the counterpart of Lemma~\ref{lem:local} there has two further parts and the event of Section~\ref{sec:norm-event}, on which Lemma~\ref{lem:contact} holds, is defined differently; several proofs differ. No formal proof uses \texttt{sorry} or an axiom beyond the three standard axioms \texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice} and \texttt{Quot.sound}. The development is at \url{https://github.com/nitromannitol/Centrally-Excited-Random-Walk}.
last_prose_only_revision.new: The theorems, lemmas and propositions of this paper were formalized in Lean~4, building on Mathlib. The formal statements are those of this paper, and the formal proofs follow its arguments. No formal proof uses \texttt{sorry} or an axiom beyond the three standard axioms \texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice} and \texttt{Quot.sound}. The development is at \url{https://github.com/nitromannitol/Centrally-Excited-Random-Walk}.
